description: Envoy Gateway data plane and control plane overview. Counterpart to the NGINX / Ingress controller dashboard.

panels.description: Downstream requests/s accepted by the selected Envoy proxies (HTTP connection manager level).
panels.title: Gateway Request Volume

panels.description: Active downstream connections.
panels.title: Gateway Connections

panels.description: CDS updates accepted per minute — the Envoy analogue of an nginx config reload.
panels.title: xDS Config Updates

panels.description: Rejected CDS + LDS updates in the last 5m. Non-zero means the proxy is running stale config.
panels.title: Failed xDS Updates

panels.description: Per-route request rate. One Envoy cluster == one HTTPRoute rule (httproute/<namespace>/<name>/rule/<n>).
panels.title: Route Request Volume

panels.description: Downstream response codes by class. Stacked, so the total height is the overall request rate and each band is one class.
panels.title: HTTP Status Classes

panels.description: Reported by Envoy itself (envoy_server_memory_*), no cAdvisor join required.
panels.title: Average Memory Usage

panels.description: Envoy exports no process CPU stat, so this comes from cAdvisor (kubelet). Requires container metrics in the same Prometheus.
panels.title: Average CPU Usage

panels.description: Upstream (backend-facing) latency percentiles per route. Envoy histograms are in milliseconds.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.50, sum(rate(envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_time_bucket{gateway_namespace=~"$gateway_namespace", gateway=~"$gateway", pod=~"$pod", envoy_cluster_name=~"$route"}[2m])) by (le, envoy_cluster_name))

histogram_quantile(0.90, sum(rate(envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_time_bucket{gateway_namespace=~"$gateway_namespace", gateway=~"$gateway", pod=~"$pod", envoy_cluster_name=~"$route"}[2m])) by (le, envoy_cluster_name))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_time_bucket{gateway_namespace=~"$gateway_namespace", gateway=~"$gateway", pod=~"$pod", envoy_cluster_name=~"$route"}[2m])) by (le, envoy_cluster_name))

panels.title: Route Percentile Response Times and Transfer Rates

panels.description: Total client-observed request time, including upstream time.
panels.title: Downstream Percentile Response Times

panels.description: envoy_server_days_until_first_cert_expiring is in days; multiplied by 86400 so Grafana can render it as a duration.
panels.title: Listener TLS Health and Certificate Expiry

panels.description: Current backlog in the control plane's internal message bus. Sustained growth means reconciliation is falling behind; 0 is healthy.
panels.title: Watchable Queue Depth

panels.description: Config snapshots pushed to proxies over the selected time range. Each one is a recomputed xDS config.
panels.title: xDS Snapshot Updates (range)

panels.description: Kubernetes objects the infrastructure manager wrote over the selected range (Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps for the proxy fleet).
panels.title: Resources Applied (range)

panels.description: Panics recovered in the watchable infrastructure. Must be 0 — anything else means the control plane hit a bug and kept running in an unknown state.
panels.title: Recovered Panics (range)

panels.description: How long each runner takes to handle a message off its queue. The runners are the control plane's pipeline stages (provider -> gateway-api -> xds -> infrastructure). A rising stage is the bottleneck.
panels.title: Watchable Subscribe Duration (p99 by runner)

panels.description: Events published per stage. Compare against subscribe duration: high publish volume plus rising duration is where backpressure starts.
panels.title: Watchable Publish Volume (5m)

panels.description: Status subresource writes per Gateway API kind. Constant churn on one kind usually means a resource is flapping between accepted and rejected.
panels.title: Status Updates by Kind (5m)

panels.description: Latency of status writes to the API server — a direct read on API server pressure or admission webhook delay.
panels.title: Status Update Duration (p99 by kind)

panels.description: Deletes are drawn negative. Sustained simultaneous apply and delete of the same kind means two controllers are fighting over an object.
panels.title: Resource Apply / Delete by Kind (5m)

panels.description: Config pushes per proxy node. One node updating far more than its peers points at a gateway whose config keeps being recomputed.
panels.title: xDS Snapshot Updates by Node (5m)

panels.description: xDS streams are long-lived, so this is normally flat at 0. Repeated closures mean proxies are reconnecting to the control plane — check control-plane restarts or network policy before trusting any data-plane config.
panels.title: Completed xDS Streams (5m)
